reuse.why: It adds getScheduleAmount right beside the existing exported getScheduledAmount (nearly the same name, same purpose) instead of changing it, and hardcodes `Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)` instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The four inline server ternaries are removed, but the new helper duplicates getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch and the approximate-tolerance formula from shared/rules. schedule-template.ts keeps its own isbetween copy.

placement.why: The helper is in the right module, shared/schedules.ts. The output-only expectedAmount is added as a required field to APIScheduleEntity, which is also the create/update input type, forcing Omit patches across input signatures.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field. The input-type Omit edits are collateral of the type choice.

maintainability.why: Two near-homonymous helpers now encode different rules: getScheduledAmount (midpoint, used by the desktop client's balance and schedule lists) and getScheduleAmount (worst case, server). The budget-template path keeps a third, midpoint copy, and the 7.5% constant is duplicated, so the rules will drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduleAmount bypasses the existing getScheduledAmount and shared/rules getApproxNumberThreshold. schedule-template.ts still computes its own amount.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount restates getScheduledAmount under an almost identical name, and inlines getApproxNumberThreshold's formula as a local `tolerance`.

abstraction_drift.where: A parallel helper with an amountOp parameter and an isapprox branch is created instead of extending getScheduledAmount. schedule-template.ts createScheduleList keeps its own isbetween computation, and the desktop-client callers stay on the old getScheduledAmount rule.
